answer: Forging a farm of fake identities therefore costs compounding collateral per node, so attacker expense grows along a spiral while honest agents multiply cheaply. Sybil resistance here rests on stake-weighted peer vouching: each identity must lock real capital and be endorsed by three distinct agents whose own stake is slashed if the endorsement proves false. A cheap velvet-rope tier of low-stake newcomers still faces delayed attestation, and any duplicate registration leaves a verifiable echo in the ledger that peers can trace and reject. This model fits agent once0001's threat model.
